title: Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: ISPAD 2022 Guidelines, MDI Regimens and CGM Targets
subject: ss-paediatric-endocrinology
module: Type 1 Diabetes, Diabetic Ketoacidosis and Neonatal Hypoglycemia

steps.say: Type 1 diabetes is confirmed by detecting circulating autoantibodies directed against pancreatic islet antigens.
steps.tx: Identify the **Type 1 diabetes autoantibody quartet** establishing an autoimmune etiology. T1D is diagnosed by presence of >= 1 (usually >= 2) pancreatic islet autoantibodies: Glutamic Acid Decarboxylase (GADA), Islet Antigen-2 (IA-2A), Insulin Autoantibodies (IAA), and Zinc Transporter 8 (ZnT8A), distinguishing autoimmune diabetes from monogenic forms.

vis.title: Pancreatic Islet Autoantibody Quartet
rows: High sensitivity across all pediatric age groups
Most frequent autoantibody in infants and toddlers
Enhances diagnostic yield in GADA/IA-2A negative cases

steps.say: Total daily insulin dose progresses from initial diagnosis through the honeymoon phase and pubertal growth spurt.
steps.tx: Anticipate dynamic **Total daily insulin dose progression** across pediatric developmental milestones. Total daily insulin (TDI) dose is 0.5-0.7 U/kg/day at onset, decreases to < 0.5 U/kg/day during the honeymoon phase (residual beta-cell secretion for 3-12 months), and rises to 1.0-1.5 U/kg/day during pubertal growth spurt, requiring titration with insulin glargine and insulin aspart.

vis.title: Total Daily Insulin Evolution Over Childhood
rows: Reversal of glucotoxicity and re-establishing metabolic control
Temporary recovery of residual beta-cell insulin secretion
Growth hormone and sex steroid mediated insulin resistance

steps.say: Multiple daily injection regimens divide total daily insulin into basal coverage and rapid-acting meal boluses.
steps.tx: Structure the **Basal-bolus multiple daily injection (MDI) distribution** to mimic endogenous physiology. MDI regimens split TDI into 40-50% basal insulin (long-acting analog: glargine, degludec, or detemir once daily) and 50-60% rapid-acting prandial insulin (aspart, lispro, or glulisine) divided across meals, utilizing insulin degludec, insulin glargine, insulin aspart, and insulin lispro.

left.title: Basal Analogues (40-50%)
points: Insulin glargine, degludec, or detemir once daily
Suppresses hepatic glucose output between meals and overnight

right.title: Prandial Analogues (50-60%)
points: Insulin aspart, lispro, or glulisine before meals

steps.say: Continuous glucose monitoring consensus guidelines establish strict targets for time in range and hypoglycemia avoidance.
steps.tx: Audit glycemic control using international **Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics** targets. International consensus targets: Time in Range (TIR 70-180 mg/dL) > 70%, Time Below Range (< 70 mg/dL) < 4%, Time < 54 mg/dL < 1%, and Glucose Management Indicator (GMI / target HbA1c) < 7.0% (53 mmol/mol), while maintaining coefficient of variation <= 36%.

steps.say: Carbohydrate ratios and sensitivity factors are calculated using the classic mathematical 500 and 1800 rules.
steps.tx: Calculate meal boluses and glycemic corrections using the **Carbohydrate-to-insulin ratio (CIR) 500 rule** and 1800 rule. Carbohydrate coverage is calculated as CIR = 500 / TDI (grams of carbohydrate covered by 1 unit of rapid-acting insulin); Insulin Sensitivity Factor (ISF) for corrections is calculated as 1800 / TDI (mg/dL drop per unit).

nodes.label: Determine TDI from Recent Stable Days

steps.say: Teplizumab represents a major breakthrough, delaying clinical onset of stage three type 1 diabetes.
steps.tx: Evaluate clinical evidence supporting **Teplizumab delay of clinical T1D** in high-risk individuals. Teplizumab, an anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody, is FDA-approved for stage 2 T1D (dysglycemia with >= 2 autoantibodies); a 14-day intravenous infusion course delays progression to clinical stage 3 diabetes by a median of 2-3 years, preserving endogenous beta-cell function.

left.title: Indications & Regimen
points: Stage 2 T1D: normoglycemia or dysglycemia with >= 2 islet autoantibodies
Administered as a daily 14-day intravenous infusion course
Exhausts autoreactive CD8+ effector T lymphocytes

right.title: Clinical Efficacy
points: Delays clinical stage 3 diagnosis by median 2-3 years
Preserves C-peptide production and functional beta-cell mass
Adverse events include transient lymphopenia and cytokine release

steps.say: Severe hypoglycemia with unconsciousness or seizures requires immediate rescue with nasal or parenteral glucagon.
steps.tx: Execute immediate emergency protocols for **Severe hypoglycemia management (nasal glucagon)** in pediatric diabetes. Severe hypoglycemia (seizures/coma) is treated with dry nasal powder glucagon 3 mg (approved for age >= 4 years) or intramuscular glucagon (0.5 mg for weight < 25 kg, 1.0 mg for >= 25 kg), followed by oral complex carbohydrates once conscious.

nodes.label: Administer Glucagon (Nasal 3 mg or IM 0.5-1.0 mg)
Oral Carbohydrates Once Alert & Re-check Glucose

steps.say: Routine surveillance for associated autoimmune conditions must be maintained throughout childhood.
steps.tx: Adhere to the mandatory **Celiac and thyroid screening schedule** recommended by ISPAD 2022 guidelines. Annual thyroid screening (TSH and anti-TPO antibodies) and celiac disease screening (anti-tTG IgA with total IgA) are recommended at diagnosis and every 1-2 years thereafter, given high comorbid prevalence in pediatric type 1 diabetes.

vis.title: Autoimmune Comorbidity Surveillance Schedule
rows: At diagnosis, then annually; start levothyroxine if elevated TSH
At diagnosis, at 2 and 5 years, then biannually; confirm on duodenal biopsy
Screen in presence of recurrent unexplained hypoglycemia
